article:
ON Semiconductor stock steadies as investors weigh valuation and AI power transition
Published on 08/29/2026 at 14:28 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
ON Semiconductor stock trades in the low-$70s as of late August 2026, with investors balancing its automotive and industrial power strengths against a softer broader chip tape and a valuation still supported by recent earnings and consensus targets.

ON Semiconductor Corp. (ISIN US6821891035) stock is trading in the low-$70s region as of late August 2026, leaving investors to weigh its positioning in power and automotive semiconductors against a broader sector pullback and a still-supportive consensus valuation backdrop.
Per recent market data as of August 28, 2026, ON Semiconductor shares closed on the Nasdaq around the mid-$70s mark, with intraday moves captured in a session where major chip names pressured US indexes and individual names such as NVIDIA and Arm Holdings posted declines of more than 4 percent and over 6 percent, respectively.
A portfolio disclosure filed by a large asset manager on August 29, 2026 shows a stake size in ON Semiconductor stock valued at $486.25 million based on a share price of $72.61, underlining how institutional investors still hold sizable positions in the name even after the sector’s latest volatility.
Institutional positioning and consensus view
The August 29, 2026 portfolio filing highlights that ON Semiconductor shares opened that trading day at $72.61 on the Nasdaq, giving the company a market value in the tens of billions of dollars and situating the stock in the mid-cap to large-cap segment of the US semiconductor universe.
According to that same filing’s use of consensus data, the current average analyst rating on ON Semiconductor stands in the moderate buy range, with a cited consensus price target of $97.04 that sits distinctly above the recent $72.61 quote and implies upside potential of roughly one third from that level if forecasts are met.
The contrast between the $72.61 opening price and the $97.04 consensus target highlights a key valuation narrative for investors: the stock is trading clearly below the level that sell-side models currently project, even as shorter-term sector sentiment has compressed multiples and driven notable single-session declines across several US chip names.
Recent trading action and sector backdrop
Market coverage of the August 28, 2026 Nasdaq session shows ON Semiconductor shares moving lower during the afternoon and into the later evening, with reported declines of 1.6 percent and then 3.3 percent as the price moved from $73.64 down to $72.32 while broader sector indices also traded weakly.
Those intraday moves place ON Semiconductor stock in a context where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 2.69 percent on the day, while large-cap peers such as NVIDIA dropped 4.57 percent and Arm Holdings declined 6.33 percent, suggesting that the name’s slide is part of a wider consolidation phase in US-listed chip equities.
For investors focused on relative performance, such data points show ON Semiconductor trading down by low-single-digit percentage moves in step with sector indices rather than diverging sharply, which may support a view that stock-specific fundamentals remain intact even as the broader group undergoes technical digestion after prior gains.
Fundamentals, earnings cycle and guidance context
Across major market-data portals, the latest trailing twelve-month view for ON Semiconductor as of late August 2026 shows revenue of $7.38 billion and net income attributable to common shareholders of $1.76 billion, translating into diluted earnings per share of $4.03 when divided by the weighted average share count.
While these trailing figures summarize performance over the last four quarters rather than a single period, they still place ON Semiconductor in a profitable and cash-generative position, with EPS in the low-single-digit dollars range and net income representing a substantial fraction of annual sales, a combination that supports ongoing investment in capacity and research for high-growth segments such as automotive and industrial power.
Relative to prior years when ON Semiconductor was transitioning its portfolio away from commodity segments and toward higher-margin intelligent power and sensing solutions, the current trailing revenue and earnings profile indicates that this transformation is now well advanced, with the company harvesting benefits from a focus on electric vehicles, renewable energy infrastructure and factory automation demand.
Using the trailing twelve-month EPS figure of $4.03 and the recent $72.61 share price cited in the August 29, 2026 filing, investors can derive an implied price-to-earnings multiple in the high teens range, signaling that the market is assigning ON Semiconductor a valuation premium versus low-growth industrial names but a discount versus the highest-multiple design and GPU specialists.
Set against the consensus price target of $97.04 from the same dataset, that P/E-based lens suggests that analysts are willing to model either continued EPS expansion or a re-rating toward a higher earnings multiple as ON Semiconductor deepens its exposure to structural themes such as vehicle electrification and power-efficient data centers.
Historically, prior fiscal years when ON Semiconductor was more heavily weighted to legacy discrete components and consumer markets tended to produce lower growth and thinner margins, so the current trailing mix of $7.38 billion in revenue and $1.76 billion in net income arguably reflects a more focused strategic posture that the market is now in the process of repricing.
Automotive and industrial power portfolio
ON Semiconductor’s core business today revolves around supplying power semiconductors, analog ICs and sensing solutions into automotive and industrial end markets, including traction inverters, on-board chargers, battery management and advanced driver-assistance systems for electric and hybrid vehicles.
In industrial settings, the company provides power devices and modules that enable efficient motor control, industrial drives and power conversion for factory automation and robotics, aligning its portfolio with customers that are upgrading equipment to increase energy efficiency and integrate more sensing and connectivity.
This strategic focus on power management, rather than commodity memory or general-purpose logic, positions ON Semiconductor to benefit from secular trends such as rising semiconductor content per vehicle and the build-out of renewable energy and storage installations, even when cyclical swings in broader chip demand temporarily pressure valuations and trading ranges.
Representative product: intelligent power solutions
A representative example of ON Semiconductor’s offering in this landscape is its intelligent power module solutions for automotive traction inverters and industrial motor drives, which integrate power devices, gate drivers and protection functions in compact, thermally optimized packages tailored to OEM design requirements.
These intelligent power modules are designed to help vehicle manufacturers and industrial equipment makers improve efficiency, reduce system complexity and shorten design cycles, leveraging ON Semiconductor’s expertise in wide bandgap materials, packaging and power electronics to deliver high-current, high-voltage solutions.
For investors, such products illustrate the company’s pivot toward complex, system-level power solutions that capture more value than simple discrete components, reinforcing why the market’s valuation debate tends to center on long-term demand for electrification and automation rather than short-term fluctuations in consumer device shipments.
With ON Semiconductor stock trading around the low-$70s mark as of the August 28-29, 2026 window and consensus price targets sitting just above $97, the shares currently occupy a zone where sector-wide volatility intersects with a still-supportive fundamental story grounded in power semiconductors and automotive content growth.
Investors who follow the name closely are likely to keep monitoring upcoming quarterly earnings and any updates to guidance, looking for confirmation that revenue and EPS trends remain aligned with the longer-term secular themes that underpin the current valuation framework and institutional interest in the stock.
